first_impression: A polished Gatehouse bug-report page shows a target version, reproduction editor, differential-run controls, and a disabled local approval step.
action_attempted: Clicked Run bad vs good with the default failing assertion.
after_state: No run result appeared because the page reported WEBMCP UNAVAILABLE and document.modelContext missing; the draft remained unrun and approval stayed disabled.
notes: The page clearly explains the gated workflow, but the central run cannot execute in this browser without WebMCP.

first_impression: A Spanish/English Colombian corner-store catalog presents products, tax classifications, destinations, shipping, payment rails, DIAN validation, and an 11-tool WebMCP surface.
after_state: The cart accepted the item and the page's commerce workflow remained available; the browser still showed 0 of 11 tools because document.modelContext was unavailable.
notes: The storefront works with its own controls, but agent tool registration is explicitly unavailable in this browser.

first_impression: TermLens offers local contract loading, agent term proposals, per-term approval, an approved summary, and audit receipts with a write-lock.
action_attempted: Loaded the sample contract and clicked Simulate Agent.
after_state: A 210-word contract loaded and three propose_term calls were logged with staged terms and confidences 0.98, 0.98, and 0.81; no terms were approved automatically.
notes: The page clearly states WebMCP is unsupported here, while the local simulated workflow still demonstrates staging and gating.

first_impression: Terrain presents a map-first local-business lead pipeline with discovery-oriented marketing copy and Get started/Pricing calls to action.
after_state: The app navigated to a Sign in page requiring email and password, with Google sign-in and sign-up options.
notes: The central workspace could not be tested without credentials; no personal data or account was entered.

first_impression: An elaborate ASCII shrine/gallery loads with many themed artworks, model filters, room controls, and clickable pieces inviting the visitor to step closer.
